title: From Holo Pockets to Electron Density: GPT-style Drug Design with Density
claim: Prior methods condition generation on an empty rigid pocket; ours conditions on a density derived from the filler, retaining richer binding context.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right arrows, blue vs green rounded boxes
description: The figure has two horizontal rows that both start from a shared Holo complex image at top left. This image shows a protein pocket surface, a bound ligand in sticks, and red solvent dots. In the top row, a black arrow leads to an Empty pocket, which is a grey surface with the ligand removed. A second arrow leads to Drug design, where a generated ligand sits in the pocket. This row is inside a blue rounded box. A long elbow arrow runs down the left side to the bottom row, inside a green rounded box. That row runs Filler (ligand plus red solvent dots), then ED (a sparse colored point cloud), then Drug design (a green generated molecule overlaid on the density points). The bold titles and the two colored boxes draw the eye first.
caption: Comparison between pocket-based drug design (blue-circled region) and our electron density (ED)-based drug design framework (green-circled region). The red dots denote the solvent. Filler is defined as all elements within a $4.5\text{\AA{}}$ radius of the ligand, excluding the binding pocket.
abstract: Recent advances in generative modeling have enabled significant progress in structure-based drug design (SBDD). Existing methods typically condition molecule generation on empty binding pockets from holo complexes, overlooking informative components such as the filler (ligands and solvent). Here, we leverage low-resolution electron density (ED) derived from the filler as a physically grounded condition for \textit{de novo} drug design. We consider two types of ED, calculated and cryo-EM/X-ray, obtainable from computational or experimental sources, supporting unified pre-training and experimental integration. Compared with rigid pocket representations, experimental ED naturally captures conformational flexibility and provides a more faithful description of the binding environment. Based on this, we introduce EDMolGPT, a decoder-only autoregressive framework that generates molecules from low-resolution ED point clouds. By grounding generation in physically meaningful density signals, EDMolGPT mitigates structural bias and produces molecules with 3D conformations. Evaluations on 101 biological targets verify the effectiveness. Our project page: https://jiahaochen1.github.io/EDMolGPT_Page/.
